repair_rounds: reality review: Mark Cuban's attention pattern: The compiled world assigns Mark Cuban 'continuously attentive' to email 24/7. The evidence says he reads/skims nearly all emails on his phone, but that does not mean he is continuously checking every second. A more faithful pattern would be frequent but not continuous checking (e.g., every 15-30 minutes during waking hours). Continuous attention distorts reality by making him notice the email instantly, which pre-writes a faster response timeline than realistic. (fix: Change Mark Cuban's email attention to a realistic pattern, e.g., 'every 15 minutes during 07:00-23:00 America/Chicago, days [0,1,2,3,4,5,6]' based on typical phone-checking habits of a busy executive.)

reality review: Spam filter exclusion: The world declares spam filtering excluded, but the evidence does not support that the email will definitely reach the inbox. Mark Cuban receives 700-1000 emails daily; many are likely filtered. Excluding spam filtering assumes delivery, which pre-writes a favorable condition for a reply. This is a material distortion because if the email is filtered, no reply is possible. (fix: Either model a realistic spam filter (e.g., a probability of delivery based on typical cold email filter rates) or add an uncertainty that the email may be filtered. Do not assume delivery.)

reality review: Pre-scheduled email sending: The world schedules the email send as a fixed event at 2026-07-27T14:00:00+00:00. This pre-writes the action instead of letting Jordan Reyes decide to send it via the actor model. While the evidence says he intends to send it that day, the exact time is not specified; scheduling it at a precise time removes the actor's agency and could affect timing of notice. (fix: Remove the scheduled send and instead let Jordan Reyes's actor model decide to send the email on July 27, using the universal transmit_information action. The intention can be a belief that drives the decision.)

reality review: Jordan Reyes has no attention pattern, no scheduled wake, and no watch: Jordan Reyes must be able to notice information (e.g., the window start notification) to decide to send the email. Without any attention pattern, the simulation will never have him act, making a reply impossible for a mechanical reason unrelated to reality. (fix: Add an attention pattern for Jordan Reyes on email, e.g., checks every 30 minutes during waking hours, or a scheduled wake at the time he intends to send the email.)
